title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 52
paragraphs: To this Xerxes replied: “Artabanus, of all the opinions you have uttered, in this one you are most mistaken — in fearing that the Ionians might change sides. Of them we have a most certain proof, of which you yourself are witness, and the others too who went with Darius on his march against the Scythians — namely this, that the whole Persian army came to depend upon these men, whether to destroy it or save it, and they showed themselves just and faithful, and did nothing at all unfriendly. Besides this, they have left their children, wives, and possessions in our land, so we must not even imagine that they will rebel. Do not fear this thing either, but be of good heart and keep safe my house and my government; for to you of all men I entrust my sceptre of rule.”
